subject: POC trial: model selection & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Ramos <diego@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: POC objectives & model options

Thanks again for the call this morning, Diego — good discussion and great context on where Acme Health wants to take this. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap proposed success criteria, the high-level evaluation plan, timeline, and suggested models for the trial so we can align on ownership and next steps.

POC goal (3 weeks): validate model quality and performance for clinical triage assistant in English and Spanish, and estimate unit costs at projected throughput (~200 concurrent users).

Success criteria (pass/fail checkpoints):
- Intent accuracy >= 92% on sampled clinical triage intents (measured on held-out dataset)
- Hallucination rate < 3% on knowledge-check prompts (failure = factually incorrect guidance)
- End-to-end median generation latency < 350ms at a target batch size (as-run numbers)
- Multilingual: Spanish responses should have equivalent accuracy within 5 percentage points of English
- Business: estimated cost per 1k tokens <= $X (we'll quantify after we get sample payloads)

Model selection (initial):
- Primary candidate: Llama-3-13B-chat (quantized 4-bit where applicable) — best balance of quality/latency for instruction-following.
- Cost-focused candidate: Mistral-7B-instruct (lower token cost, useful as fallback).
- Multilingual/fallback: use translate-then-prompt with a small XLM-R based translator for Spanish heavy traffic, or evaluate a multilingual variant of Llama if needed.

Evaluation plan (attached: poc-eval-plan.xlsx):
- Week 0: ingest sample dataset (you provide) + stake holder sign-off on test prompts
- Week 1: run baseline evals (accuracy, hallucination, latency) on Llama-3 & Mistral variants
- Week 2: tune prompts/caching, run workload-style latency tests, and produce cost estimates
- Week 3: final results + recommended rollout plan and next steps (Dedicated or Hosted config)

Ownership / next steps proposed:
- Acme (Diego): share sample data (anonymized) & expected traffic profile by EOD 2026-08-16
- Redwood (Ben): provision trial instances, run evals, and deliver results; will also provide inference cost spreadsheet
- Redwood (Marissa): program owner for the POC, coordinate stakeholder reviews & commercial follow-up

Attachments: 20260812-poc-eval-plan.xlsx (evaluation matrix & sample prompts)

If that looks right, confirm and we'll schedule the kick-off (Ben and I can join your engineering sync next week).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Multilingual importance: Spanish is a hard requirement for all triage flows (roughly 20% of traffic). We'd prefer a single-model solution if quality is comparable, but fallback translate-then-prompt is acceptable if it keeps latency in check.
2) Timeframe: 3-week POC works for us; can we aim to have initial results by the week of Aug 24?
3) Data: we'll provide ~1k anonymized transcripts + 200 labeled intents by Aug 16. Priya (cc'd) will own delivery.
4) Infrastructure question: are the trial instances hosted on Redwood's Hosted API or do you spin up a dedicated sandbox for us? We need to understand any IP/data residency implications.

Also: can you include an explicit fallback model recommendation for Spanish (if single-model doesn't meet threshold)?

— Diego

diego@acmehealth.com

Great notes — adding some technical detail and a concrete recommendation from the SE side.

Quick answers:
- Trial infra: we can run the POC on Redwood Hosted API under a trial tenant (normal for initial evals) or spin up an isolated Dedicated sandbox if you require stronger isolation / network controls. For Acme's usage and data residency notes, we recommend Hosted trial first to get results quickly; if needed we'll move to Dedicated for any sensitive workloads.

Model recommendation (concrete):
- Primary: Llama-3-13B-chat (4-bit quantized) — expect strong instruction following and good English quality. We'll run both the full-precision and quantized variants to check quality delta.
- Fallback/cost alternative: Mistral-7B-instruct — significantly lower token cost, slightly lower quality; useful for bursty/low-cost routes.
- Spanish fallback: if a single-model approach (Llama-3 multilingual variant) doesn't meet the Spanish accuracy delta, we'll use a small translation step (open-source MarianMT or m2m100) + the Llama model for core generation. Translation-first approach typically adds ~30–60ms but keeps generation quality high. We'll validate latency budget during Week 2.

Evaluation details (I'll run these):
- Accuracy/hallucination: run held-out labeled set (200 examples) and an additional 300 sample prompts from production transcripts.
- Latency: scripted load test to approximate 200 concurrent users, measure p50/p90/p99 for generation and overall end-to-end.
- Cost: attachment included (inference-cost-estimates.csv) with per-model token estimates for hosted vs quantized paths.

Milestones & tentative dates:
- Aug 16: Acme shares sample data (Priya)
- Aug 18: Redwood provisions trial tenant + baseline evals completed
- Aug 24: Tune + workload tests completed; present preliminary results
- Aug 28: Final report + recommendation

Next steps for Acme (action items):
1) Share anonymized transcripts and expected traffic profile (Priya)
2) Provide a short list of must-have intents for bench marking (200 labeled examples)

I'll start a sandbox env once we get the data.

Ben Carter
